articles.title: ‘KL is klutch’: Delhi Capitals put KL Rahul trade rumours to bed with blunt message
articles.summary: Cricket News: Delhi Capitals have put an end to speculation surrounding KL Rahul’s future, making it clear that the wicketkeeper-batter remains an important part of.
articles.body: Delhi Capitals have put an end to speculation surrounding KL Rahul’s future, making it clear that the wicketkeeper-batter remains an important part of their plans and is not heading to any other franchise.Rumours about a potential trade involving Rahul had gathered momentum on social media over the past two weeks, Neither the franchise nor Rahul had officially addressed the speculation until Delhi Capitals co-owner Parth Jindal broke his silence.Jindal made it clear that Delhi have no intention of parting ways with Rahul, highlighting both his performances and his selfless approach to the team.“KL IS KLUTCH FOR @DelhiCapitals - one of the nicest guys I know and one who puts the team before himself always. We have unfinished business and will work hard together to make Delhi proud @IPL,” Jindal wrote on X (formerly Twitter).Rahul responded to Jindal’s post, seemingly putting any doubts over his future to rest.“Thank you, can't wait for the coming season,” the Indian batter wrote.The speculation surrounding Rahul gained traction after Delhi added Rishabh Pant to their squad earlier this year, having traded Kuldeep Yadav to Lucknow Super Giants (LSG).The arrival of Pant means Delhi now have two established wicketkeeping options, while both players have experience of leading teams. Axar Patel remains another leadership option, although his position could come under scrutiny following Delhi's disappointing results in the 2025 and 2026 editions.Despite that combination, Jindal's comments suggest Delhi see Rahul as central to their plans rather than someone they are looking to move on.Rahul has also provided the franchise with considerable consistency since joining them. In his first two seasons with Delhi, he crossed the 1,000-run mark, establishing himself as one of their most reliable batters at the top of the order.With Pant expected to take over the wicketkeeping responsibilities, Rahul could now have greater freedom to focus solely on his batting. That could also open the possibility of the two India stars forming an opening partnership for Delhi.The speculation intensified despite the absence of any official indication that a trade was being discussed. Delhi eventually responded to the noise by posting a video with the caption, “Keep the noise coming.”Jindal's latest post, however, has offered a much more direct response.Rahul is coming off a productive 2026 campaign in which he scored 593 runs for Delhi, finishing fourth in the tournament's run-scoring charts. His standout performance came against Shreyas Iyer's Punjab Kings at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, where he smashed an unbeaten 152, the highest individual score by an Indian in the league.Rahul's innings contained nine sixes and came at a strike rate of 226.9, although Delhi's huge total was ultimately chased down by Punjab Kings.For now, though, the message from Delhi is clear: Rahul remains part of their plans, with Jindal insisting that the franchise still has “unfinished business” with the senior batter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Melbourne Renegades first team up for sale as Big Bash opens door for private investment in historic move; what it means
articles.summary: Cricket News: Cricket Australia (CA) has opened the door to private investment in the Big Bash League (BBL), with the Melbourne Renegades set to become the first fr.
articles.body: Cricket Australia (CA) has opened the door to private investment in the Big Bash League (BBL), with the Melbourne Renegades set to become the first franchise offered for sale from the 2027-28 season.The decision comes after months of discussions between Cricket Australia and Australia's state cricket associations over the future of the domestic T20 competition.At a press conference at the SCG on Tuesday afternoon, CA confirmed that the Renegades will be the first BBL franchise to enter the private ownership process. Other BBL and WBBL teams could also be offered for sale in the future under a “self-determination” model.The governing body said the move is aimed at bringing private investment into the T20 competition and strengthening the financial position of Australian cricket as players and teams are increasingly being drawn towards lucrative leagues around the world."CA will invite bids from private owners for the Renegades with a view to them playing the 2027-28 season under new ownership," the governing body said in a statement on Tuesday."Beginning the sales process for the Renegades allows us to take the first step in a self-determination model for our members and represents a defining moment for the game," said Cricket Australia chair Mike Baird."This is a significant decision that has involved an enormous amount of analysis, discussion and collaboration over many months."CA said other franchises could be put on the market at a later stage."Pending the result of that process, CA will consider taking other clubs to market under a self-determination model that gives each state member the ability to assess the optimal pathway for its own club and community."According to cricket.com.au, Hobart Hurricanes, Perth Scorchers and Melbourne Stars are among the other clubs believed to be interested in private investment.The Renegades are owned by Cricket Victoria, which supported CA's original plan. They won the BBL title in the 2018-19 season.The move comes as CA looks to strengthen its finances. Despite a boost in revenue from hosting a five-Test series against India, the game's biggest financial market, CA reported a net deficit of A$11.3 million for the 2024-25 financial year."By opening the door to private investment in the Big Bash Leagues, Cricket Australia is taking a deliberate step to strengthen and secure the long-term future of the game," CA Chairman Mike Baird said in Tuesday's statement.Australia Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced in July that December's BBL 2026-27 season opener between the Renegades and Perth Scorchers would take place in the Chennai.While CA is allowing private ownership, it will continue to control key areas of the competition. Baird said the governing body will retain control over international scheduling, player availability, salary caps and media rights.CA will also have the power to approve or veto investors and set a reserve price for the sale.Any changes to a club's name, colours or branding will also require approval. For the Melbourne Renegades, CA will be the approving authority, while the relevant state body will have that role for the other teams.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Phones confiscated, players sent home: Pakistan's England tour turmoil revives memories of Mohammad Amir, Salman Butt and Mohammad Asif's 2010 Lord's spot-fixing scandal
articles.summary: Cricket News: England has not often been a happy place for Pakistan cricket in recent times. In the ongoing three-Test series, Pakistan have already lost the first .
articles.body: England has not often been a happy place for Pakistan cricket in recent times. In the ongoing three-Test series, Pakistan have already lost the first two matches by big margins. They suffered an innings defeat in the series opener at Headingley before losing the second Test at Lord's by 194 runs. The third Test is set to begin at Edgbaston on Wednesday.However, what followed the defeat at Lord's surprised even those familiar with the unpredictable nature of Pakistan cricket.The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sent seven players home and called up another seven, with five of the replacements uncapped at Test level.The PCB also removed Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. They were replaced by Pakistan's white-ball coaches Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke.Salman Ali Agha, who captained Pakistan at Headingley in the absence of the injured Babar Azam, was among those sent home. Left-arm spinner Ali Usman, who took a five-wicket haul in that Test, was also released.Experienced wicketkeeper Mohammad Rizwan and opener Imam-ul-Haq were also told to leave. Imam did not bat in either innings at Lord's because of a calf injury.Hesson admitted last week that the changes had added to the uncertainty around the team."The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. I don't think anyone wants this to happen in the middle of a series."The situation took another turn on Monday when the PCB announced an investigation into the squad's conduct during the England tour, bringing the issue of match-fixing back into focus.As reported by TimesofIndia.com, the changes within Pakistan cricket were driven by reasons that were “more than cricket” and were not simply a response to the team's poor performances.According to Pakistani outlet 365 News, the players' devices have been handed over to the PCB and will remain in the board's custody until the final Test is completed. The report did not reveal which players had their phones taken, while the PCB has not publicly explained why the devices were confiscated.Horror of 2010The developments have also brought back memories of Pakistan's 2010 spot-fixing scandal, one of the biggest corruption cases in cricket.The scandal took place during Pakistan's tour of England, during the fourth Test at Lord's. It centred on allegations that Pakistani players had deliberately bowled no-balls at specific points in the match in return for money.When Mohammad Amir overstepped the crease while bowling a no-ball against England on the opening day of the 2010 Lord's Test, there was no indication that the moment would become part of a fixing scandal that would affect Pakistan cricket for years.Two days later, it emerged that three no-balls — two by Amir and one by his pace partner Mohammad Asif — were part of a betting deal.Pakistan captain Salman Butt had arranged the deliberate no-balls in return for money offered by undercover journalist Mazhar Majeed, who was posing as a bookmaker.The scandal, exposed in the sting by Britain's now-defunct News of the World tabloid, rocked the cricketing world , and aftershocks can still be felt more than a decade on in Pakistan. Not only did that dark morning at the revered 'home of cricket' derail the careers of three players who were banned and jailed, the saga also led to calls for Pakistan to be booted from international cricket. Butt, Amir and Asif were tried in a London court for offences under the Gambling Act and were jailed in November 2011.Announcing the sentences, the judge underscored the severity of the crime. “The image and integrity of what was once a game, but is now a business, is damaged in the eyes of all, including the many youngsters who regarded three of you as heroes,” Justice Jeremy Cooke said. It marked a new low for Pakistan cricket, already reeling from the aftermath of terror attacks in Lahore on the Sri Lankan team a year before, which triggered the suspension of home internationals.In November 2011, after a high-profile trial in London, all three players were found guilty of corruption and conspiracy to accept illegal payments. Salman Butt received a 30-month prison sentence, Mohammad Asif was jailed for a year, and Mohammad Amir, due to his age and early confession, was sentenced to six months.Only one of them, Amir, returned to international cricket after serving the ICC-ban when he made his comeback in 2016.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s sharp cricket brain shines! 15-year-old plots two big wickets in Duleep Trophy final – Watch
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation is already showing the tactical awareness of a seasoned cricketer. The East .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation is already showing the tactical awareness of a seasoned cricketer. The East Zone vice-captain played a key role in two crucial dismissals as his side tightened the screws on South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.After East Zone piled up a mammoth 708, largely courtesy of captain Ishan Kishan’s magnificent 270, South Zone appeared to be settling into their reply. But Sooryavanshi’s sharp reading of the game helped East Zone strike twice before tea on Day 3.Sooryavanshi trusts his instinct for crucial DRS callThe first breakthrough came when Ricky Bhui appeared to have survived a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar. The pacer zipped one down the leg side as Bhui attempted to guide it away, but the on-field umpire remained unmoved despite the appeal.Sooryavanshi, however, was convinced there was something behind it. The teenager urged Kishan to take the Decision Review System (DRS), and his instinct proved spot on.UltraEdge showed a spike as the ball passed the bat, with wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra completing the catch to send Bhui back.BCCI also highlighted Sooryavanshi’s intervention on social media.“Take it... take it. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi urges the captain to take the review, and it turns out to be successful,” BCCI wrote, while sharing the video of the dismissal on X.It was another example of the youngster’s growing influence in senior cricket. His ability to make the call under pressure was particularly impressive.Teenage vice-captain brings Shami back at the perfect timeSooryavanshi’s tactical contribution did not end with the DRS call.With South Zone at 174/4 and only minutes remaining before tea, the youngster was temporarily standing in as captain after Kishan went off the field. He decided to bring Mohammed Shami back for a short burst despite the veteran pacer having already bowled a demanding spell.Shami had earlier walked off after bowling seven overs and had bowled only twice after lunch. He had also required treatment to his neck from the physio.Yet Sooryavanshi recognised the opportunity to use the experienced seamer for a quick spell before the interval.The move paid immediate dividends.Shami dismissed Smaran Ravichandran, the highest run-scorer of the previous Ranji Trophy season, when the Karnataka batter chased a delivery outside off and nicked it behind. The on-field umpire again did not give the batter out, but this time Kushagra urged Sooryavanshi to review.UltraEdge once again confirmed the edge.Ravichandran was gone, South Zone were reduced to 176/5, and Sooryavanshi had played a direct role in two of East Zone’s most important wickets.DRS instinct becoming a Sooryavanshi trademarkThe decision-making has not been a one-off for Sooryavanshi in this Duleep Trophy campaign.During East Zone’s semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru, the youngster made another bold DRS call after Aryan Juyal was initially given not out following a caught-behind appeal against Mukesh Kumar.Juyal, batting on 46, pushed hard at a delivery outside off and the East Zone players immediately appealed. When the umpire rejected the appeal, there was some hesitation among the fielders over whether to review.Sooryavanshi trusted his instinct and called for the review at the last moment. UltraEdge detected a spike, confirming the edge and handing East Zone a crucial wicket.The youngster had also spoken about his willingness to contribute with the ball during the tournament, joking that he considered himself a “wicket-taker”.“Opponent team's wickets weren't falling, so I was asked to bowl two or three overs. Ishan Bhaiya felt like he was taking a risk, but he didn't know that I am a wicket-taker,” Sooryavanshi said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic.His batting may have made him one of Indian cricket’s most talked-about teenage prospects, but his Duleep Trophy campaign is increasingly showcasing another side of his game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill turns 27: 10 records that chart his rise from prodigy to record-breaking India captain
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shubman Gill has already packed an impressive collection of records into his career, and the India captain has another milestone to celebrate as he tu.
articles.body: Shubman Gill has already packed an impressive collection of records into his career, and the India captain has another milestone to celebrate as he turns 27 today.From rewriting ODI batting records to producing a historic Test series as captain, Gill has continued to make his mark across formats. His rise has been particularly striking in recent years, with the right-hander establishing himself as one of India’s key batters while taking on the leadership role in both Tests and ODIs.As Gill begins his 27th year, here are 10 standout records that underline his remarkable journey so far.1. Fastest Indian to 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 ODI runsGill holds the record for being the fastest Indian to reach 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 ODI runs. He reached 1,000 runs in 19 innings, 2,000 in 38 innings and 3,000 in 62 innings. His 38-innings mark for 2,000 ODI runs is also the fastest by any batter in the history of the format.2. Youngest ODI double-century scorerGill became the youngest player to score an ODI double century when he smashed an unbeaten 208 off 149 balls against New Zealand in January 2023. He was only 23 years and 132 days old at the time, producing one of the most memorable innings of his young international career.3. Highest IPL playoff scoreGill holds the record for the highest individual score in IPL playoff history. He produced a sensational 129 off just 60 balls for Gujarat Titans against Mumbai Indians in Qualifier 2 during the 2023 season, powering his side to a commanding victory.4. Youngest to Reach 4,000 IPL RunsGill became the youngest batter to reach 4,000 runs in IPL history. He achieved the feat during the 2026 season at the age of 26 years and 216 days.5. Most runs by an Indian in a Test matchGill produced a historic performance during India's tour of England, scoring 269 and 161 in the Edgbaston Test. His combined tally of 430 runs is the highest aggregate by an Indian batter in a single Test match. Overall, it is the second-highest aggregate in Test history, behind England's Graham Gooch, who scored 456 against India at Lord's in 1990.6. Biggest away Test win by an Indian captainGill also recorded a historic achievement as captain at Edgbaston. His side defeated England by 336 runs after setting a target of 608, making it the biggest Test victory away from home by an Indian captain in terms of runs. It was also Gill's first Test win as India's captain.7. Fourth Indian with ODI and Test double centuriesGill joined an elite group of Indian batters when he scored a double century at Edgbaston. He became only the fourth Indian after Virender Sehwag, Sachin Tendulkar and Rohit Sharma to score double centuries in both ODI and Test cricket.8. First to score four centuries in debut Test series as captainGill enjoyed a remarkable start to his tenure as India's Test captain during the England tour. He scored four centuries in the series, becoming the first player to hit four hundreds in his debut Test series as a Test captain.9. Most runs by an Indian in a three-match ODI seriesGill holds the record for the most runs by an Indian batter in a three-match ODI series. He scored 360 runs against New Zealand at home in 2023, averaging 180 at a strike rate of 128.57. His tally included two centuries.10. Five Test Centuries in first calendar year as captainGill also enjoyed a record-breaking first year as India's Test captain. He scored five centuries in Test cricket during 2025, making him one of the players with the most Test hundreds in their first calendar year as captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Duleep Trophy Final: Mohammed Shami turns the screw as South Zone stumble at 242/6, trail by 466 at stumps on day 3
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Zone’s hopes of mounting a fightback in the Duleep Trophy final took another hit on Tuesday as veteran pacer Mohammad Shami produced two crucial.
articles.body: South Zone’s hopes of mounting a fightback in the Duleep Trophy final took another hit on Tuesday as veteran pacer Mohammad Shami produced two crucial breakthroughs to leave them struggling at 242 for six at stumps on Day 3 against East Zone.Captain Tilak Varma remained unbeaten on 56 off 133 balls alongside CV Milind, but South Zone still face a daunting 466-run deficit after East piled up a mammoth 708 in their first innings. With only four wickets remaining, South have a huge task ahead to avoid the follow-on, let alone stay in contention for the title.Shami’s short spells make the differenceShami was used in short bursts throughout the day but made each spell count. The 36-year-old finished with figures of 11-4-17-2, repeatedly troubling the South Zone batters with his accuracy and movement.On a pitch where East’s bowlers had struggled to make much of an impact over the opening two days, Shami stuck to a disciplined stump-to-stump line and rarely allowed the batters room to free their arms.His first major breakthrough came when Shaik Rasheed was looking settled alongside Devdutt Padikkal. Rasheed had made 29 and the pair had added 56 for the third wicket before Shami found the perfect line to trap him in front.The veteran pacer returned much later and struck again, removing Ravichandran Smaran after the batter had built a 45-run stand with Tilak.Shami set up the left-hander beautifully, beginning with a fuller delivery on the stumps before bringing two successive balls into him. The fourth delivery moved away, taking the outside edge through to wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra. East reviewed the decision and DRS confirmed the caught-behind dismissal.Padikkal fifty goes in vainEarlier, Padikkal had looked South Zone’s most assured batter. Coming off a productive tour of Sri Lanka, the Karnataka left-hander reached his half-century in 65 balls, using his trademark composure to negotiate the East attack.But his stay ended soon after when Mukesh Kumar exploited Padikkal’s preference for the pick-up flick. A delivery on the pads invited the shot, but Padikkal failed to find the middle and holed out to substitute fielder DP Das in the deep.The wicket summed up South Zone’s day, promising partnerships repeatedly ended just when they appeared to be building momentum.South lose three in middle sessionSouth Zone had started the day with some stability after losing vice-captain Ricky Bhui early, with Narayan Jagadeesan joining Padikkal to add 60 for the second wicket.Jagadeesan looked fluent against the spinners and struck several elegant boundaries, but his aggressive approach eventually brought about his downfall. Part-time spinner Shikhar Mohan, who was brought into the attack early after Anukul Roy suffered a finger injury, bowled wide outside off.Jagadeesan attempted to cut the ball but could only produce an uppish shot that was comfortably taken by Abhimanyu Easwaran at cover. South managed only 61 runs in the second session while losing three wickets.Tilak keeps South fightingWith the innings repeatedly losing momentum, Tilak took responsibility for holding the lower order together. The South captain brought up his third consecutive fifty-plus score of the competition, reaching 56 from 133 balls. He and Shreyas Gopal then survived for 26.4 overs, adding 66 runs during the final couple of hours.Gopal eventually fell for 26 in the closing stages, leaving Tilak unbeaten with Milind at stumps. The partnership offered South some late resistance, but the bigger picture remains bleak. They trail by 466 runs and are still well short of the follow-on target, leaving East Zone firmly in control heading into the fourth day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Joe Root hits back at 'disrespectful' notion opposition have shown 'no fight' ahead of third Test
articles.summary: Joe Root has rejected the idea Pakistan have shown 'no fight' in their Test series against England; Pakistan made wholesale changes ahead of third Test; watch the third Test between England and Pakistan, at Edgbaston, live on Sky Sports from Wednesday September 9
articles.body:
Root was speaking ahead of England's third Test against Pakistan, starting on Wednesday at Edgbaston, live on Sky Sports , with England leading 2-0 in the three-match series after dominating in both Tests.

Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston.

Not only that, the Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct".

With so much disruption, Root was asked what it is like to take on a team that is offering "no fight".

For Root, that is "disrespectful" to both England and Pakistan, with the answer probably somewhere in the middle between one team playing well and one team playing poorly.

"Absolutely we have found [Pakistan] a challenge," Root said.

"I think that's a bit disrespectful to both Pakistan as a team and to us as a team. I don't think we've allowed them to get into games because of how well we've played as well and how quickly we've read the situations and the surfaces that we've had.

"I think it's very easy to say one team is excellent and one team is poor. Normally it's somewhere in the middle.

"If one team has been outstanding then the other team can't have been poor and vice versa. I think it's important to live in that middle area somewhere and understand that that's not how it is.

"Regardless of what's happened over the last two games, this week it's a completely different proposition for us.

"There's a very talented group of players in that dressing room and you've got to be ready for it, so we'll make sure that we are."

One question that will rage on following this series is whether Emilio Gay will continue as one of England's openers.

Gay has played five Tests across this summer, scoring two half-centuries along the way.

However, he is averaging around 23 with the returning Jacob Bethell and Jordan Cox touted as potential openers for the Test side.

Root says they remain hypotheticals and he is focused on this upcoming Test, but maintains it is important to put into context the runs that Gay has been scoring.

"I think Emilio has been brilliant in the conditions that we have had and I think it would be unfair to have any kind of discussions on anything outside of this game," he said.

"He has played some vital knocks and context is really important when you have low-scoring games and a low-scoring series.

"He has done really well in many respects in the hardest possible conditions."

On Monday, it was announced that Kevin Pietersen will be returning to the England set-up for the first time since 2014 as a specialist mentor to the white-ball teams in the build-up to next year's Cricket World Cup in Africa.

Pietersen will join head coach Brendon McCullum's white-ball set-up for the T20 international and ODI series' against Sri Lanka later this month, part of a coaching team that also includes Marcus Trescothick, Tim Southee, Jeetan Patel and Sarah Taylor.

Root flagged himself as the final England player still active to have featured alongside Pietersen and knows from his own experience as a youngster coming up what vital advice he can give.

"I am probably the last player to have played with him still going," Root said.

"I really enjoyed him as a senior player coming into the team. He was someone that I would be shadowing all the time.

"That first Tour of India in particular, I tried to buddy up with him in the nets, watch how he practised, watch how he did things, ask him for advice and he was really open, really honest, very helpful in terms of how to get the best out of my game against spin.

"If he can offer that kind of stuff in a coaching capacity as he did as a senior player then I think it's really going to benefit us as a group."

And asked whether Pietersen being a somewhat controversial character bothers him? Root adamantly explained that frankness is what is required at the highest level.

"I think you want people to give their honest opinion," he added.

"Why would you get him involved if you didn't want him to tell you what you think and to give his insight into the game.

"He is very knowledgeable, he has got a very good understanding of batting in particular and he's got a huge amount of energy.

"So, I think he's going to be great for the group and I'm really looking forward to getting him involved."

articles.title: Babar Azam breaks silence on Pakistan cricket’s mid-series shake-up, says 'it was news to me as well'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has broken his silence on the Pakistan Cricket Board’s sweeping mid-series shake-up, revealing that he was not consulted b.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has broken his silence on the Pakistan Cricket Board’s sweeping mid-series shake-up, revealing that he was not consulted before seven players were dropped and changes were made to the coaching setup.The PCB made the drastic changes after Pakistan suffered back-to-back heavy defeats in the Test series against England, with several established players sent home ahead of the final Test at Edgbaston.Speaking to reporters ahead of the 3rd Test match against England, Babar admitted that the developments came as a surprise even to him.'I was not consulted’Babar made it clear that the decision to overhaul the squad was taken entirely by the PCB.“It was news to me as well. I also came to know about it later. Since the PCB made the decision, they can explain it better,” Babar said in the pre-match press conference.The captain added that he was not involved in the decision to send seven players back or make changes to the coaching staff. The players released included Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Aamir Jamal, Khurram Shahzad, Ali Usman and Awais Zafar.Fit to lead at EdgbastonAmid the turmoil, Babar also confirmed that he is fit to lead Pakistan in the final Test. The captain had missed training earlier in the week after suffering from fever but has recovered in time for the Edgbaston contest. articles.title: Kevin Pietersen: Joe Root says England are 'very different' from 2014
articles.summary: Joe Root says the England team is "very different" to the one Kevin Pietersen was sacked from in 2014, after the former batter joined the coaching staff of the white-ball side.
articles.body:
Joe Root said the England team is "very different" to the one Kevin Pietersen was sacked from in 2014 after the former batter joined the coaching staff of the white-ball side.

Captain Root is the only remaining England Test player to have been in the same team as Pietersen and was on the Ashes tour of 2013-14 that signalled the end of the 46-year-old's international career.

On Monday it was announced that Pietersen will join the white-ball team as a mentor in the build-up to the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, the country of his birth.

"I'm fortunate enough to be in that position where I did play alongside him," Root told BBC Sport.

"A lot of the guys will have watched him and got into the game because of him. It will be great for those guys to have the opportunity to work alongside him."

Pietersen is one of the finest batters to ever play for England, known for his innovative strokeplay and ability to dismantle opposition bowling attacks.

His style of play across a 10-year international career was ahead of its time, much more in keeping with the batting now commonplace in modern white-ball cricket.

But 'KP' could often be a divisive figure. In 2012, he was dropped by England over allegations he sent derogatory text messages about then captain Andrew Strauss to the South Africa team.

Pietersen was reintegrated into the England team under Strauss' successor Alastair Cook. Cook's England fell apart during the 5-0 Ashes humiliation in 2013-14, after which Pietersen was dropped.

In 2015, Strauss, in his role as England director of cricket, said Pietersen would not be recalled because of a "trust issue".

Root, who played 12 Tests and nine one-day internationals alongside Pietersen, said the former Nottinghamshire, Hampshire and Surrey batter is not afraid to speak his mind.

Pietersen joins England's white-ball coaching team

KP's back - listen to the Test Match Special podcast

"That's him as a person," said Root. "When you get someone involved you want them to be themselves and you want them to come into an environment for a reason.

"With his experience and knowledge about the game, and all that he can offer, I think he's going to be great.

"You're looking at so many hypothetical things that could go wrong, when there are so many amazing things he will bring to that environment. The world is a very different place to what it was in 2014, and the England team is in a very different place to that as well."

Only Root and Cook have scored more than Pietersen's 13,779 international runs for England.

Pietersen will join Brendon McCullum's staff for the white-ball series against Sri Lanka next week, and Root highlighted the work the pair did together when the Yorkshireman was a young player.

"He was always someone who gave me a huge amount, to be honest," said Root, who made his England debut as a 21-year-old in 2012.

"He didn't need to offer as much as he did to me, but he would sit there and work tirelessly, making sure I felt comfortable with my own game. He listened to all my questions and helped as much as he could. As a senior player, he was outstanding."

Root will lead England in the third and final Test against Pakistan on Wednesday, with the home side looking for a 3-0 clean sweep in the 35-year-old's first series since returning as captain.

As with the previous two Tests, Root declined to confirm his XI ahead of the toss, though the home side are expected to be unchanged.

Since England won the second Test at Lord's, a debate has arisen about ticket prices for the home Ashes next summer.

At Edgbaston, the venue for this week's Test, Ashes tickets for the famous Hollies Stand are priced at £165 up from £125 in the same stand for the series against Australia in 2023.

"I don't know what it takes to run a county or run a venue, I don't know what goes into that," said Root. "From a playing point of view and as a captain, you want the grounds to be full, and you want them to be full of every demographic of person.

"You want the game to feel like it is for everyone, that they can come to support you and enjoy that. I don't really know what more to say on it, to be honest. It would be great to see this place full and thriving, and for everyone to have the opportunity to come to watch Test cricket."

Under Root's predecessor Ben Stokes, England developed a habit of starting Test series well but ending them poorly. England have lost the final Test in their past six consecutive multi-match series.

Root admitted only a win in Birmingham changes that record, and also had a strong defence of Stokes and former Test coach McCullum.

"We wouldn't have been able to play these last two games without all of the work those two did," he said. "I think it's undervalued the impact what those two guys had on English cricket.

"You look at where we were and how we played our cricket, you look at how we've been able to perform in the last two games, a lot of that is down to the hard work and the way they changed the mentality within English cricket and this team.

"I'm not going to sit here and have comparisons thrown against those two, I don't think that's fair whatsoever. They deserve a lot of credit for the last two performances."

articles.title: ‘Convicted or not convicted’: Wasim Akram breaks silence on Imran Khan’s health — ‘I miss him a lot’
articles.summary: Cricket News: Wasim Akram has become the latest high-profile cricketing figure to publicly voice concern over the health of his former Pakistan captain and close fr.
articles.body: Wasim Akram has become the latest high-profile cricketing figure to publicly voice concern over the health of his former Pakistan captain and close friend Imran Khan, insisting that his legal status should not come in the way of ensuring he receives proper medical care.Imran, 73, has been in jail since 2022 after being convicted in multiple corruption cases, charges he denies. Akram, however, said that while legal proceedings must take their course, there should be no compromise when it comes to his former mentor’s health.“I haven't spoken to him for three years. It's so unfortunate, politically, what's happening with him. The court of law is the court of law. But as far as his health is concerned, there can be no compromise on that,” Akram told The Athletic.The former Pakistan fast bowler also made an emotional plea while stressing that his comments were rooted in his relationship with Imran as a friend, rather than politics.“I'm speaking from the heart as someone who is worried about him as a person. Convicted or not convicted. Jail or no jail. We need to safeguard his health. We don't know what's happening, the government are saying his health apparently is fine. But I'm worried. I miss him a lot,” he said.‘Here in Pakistan? I'm not so sure’Akram also questioned whether enough was being done inside Pakistan to address concerns surrounding Imran's health, pointing to international efforts seeking better conditions for the former Pakistan captain.“There's a movement in England and elsewhere (to improve Imran's conditions) but here (in Pakistan)? I'm not so sure,” said Wasim.The comments come amid growing international concern over Imran's reported health and access to medical care. Last week, West Indies great Brian Lara joined a growing list of former international captains who have called for proper treatment and humane conditions for the 1992 World Cup-winning captain.As many as 22 international captains have written an open letter to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, seeking proper medical care and humane treatment for Imran. Australian captain Pat Cummins has also echoed the concerns, while Lara described Imran as “a legend of our game” who deserved “basic humanity”.Former Pakistan players have also spoken out. Javed Miandad made an emotional plea for Imran's release and urged the differences between the former prime minister and the government to be resolved, with Moin Khan and Ramiz Raja subsequently expressing concerns over his wellbeing.Akram also referred to an interview given by Imran's sons, Sulaiman and Kasim, during the ongoing England-Pakistan series, in which they expressed fears for their father's safety in prison.“There was a bit of uproar here [in Pakistan] after that. I then read that the Pakistani government came up with how many visits Imran has had, with all the numbers included, with all the phone calls he has had. But, you know, it's difficult to believe, and hard to know what to believe right now,” Akram said.His comments come after a court ordered Imran to be admitted to a specific hospital and allowed access to his personal physician and sister.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has announced Campa, SBI Life and ChatGPT as Associate Partners for India’s home cricket season, with the three brands signing two-season deals running through March 2028.The partnerships, which begin with India’s upcoming home series against the West Indies, have a combined value of more than Rs 130 crore. articles.body: Ricky Ponting has admitted he is worried about where ODI cricket is heading, with the former Australia captain fearing the 50-over format could gradually be squeezed out by the ever-growing presence of T20 franchise cricket across the globe.Ponting, one of the most successful ODI batters in cricket history with 13,704 runs in the format, believes the growing number of franchise competitions could leave limited room for 50-over cricket in the years ahead. While he is not happy about the prospect, he feels it could become an inevitable consequence of the changing game.‘50-over cricket is probably going to be played less’“As the months go by and the years go by and more and more T20 cricket is being played and more franchises and franchise tournaments are starting around the world, it's more and more likely that 50-over cricket is probably going to be played less. It's inevitable, which I'm not a huge fan of, to be honest,” Ponting told PTI.The former Australia skipper was speaking during an interaction facilitated by the World Championship of Legends, where he is set to be a co-owner of the Australia Champions franchise.Ponting confident about Test cricketDespite his concerns over ODIs, Ponting remains confident that Test cricket will retain its place at the top level, provided the major cricketing nations continue to prioritise the longest format. The Australian believes India, Australia, England and South Africa will play a crucial role in keeping Test cricket strong.“I love playing that format of the game, but something's got to give somewhere. articles.summary: Cricket News: KOCHI: There is a sense of deja vu around Kerala’s spin department ahead of the Ranji Trophy season. Left-arm spinner Aditya Sarwate is back, and with.
articles.body: KOCHI: There is a sense of deja vu around Kerala’s spin department ahead of the Ranji Trophy season. Left-arm spinner Aditya Sarwate is back, and with Jalaj Saxena alongside him, Kerala once again look like a team capable of dictating terms and asserting their dominance on pitches that offer even the slightest assistance.For Sarwate, 36, the return is a homecoming of sorts. He helped chalk out Kerala’s journey to the Ranji final last season, his first year with the state, when he took 36 wickets.A year later, after playing for Chhattisgarh, Sarwate returns to familiar territory.“I enjoyed my time in Kerala, when we reached the Ranji Trophy final. There was some miscommunication with the then Kerala coach Amay Khurasiya, following which I shifted to Chhattisgarh. After last season, I approached KCA, asking them if I could return, and they readily agreed,” he told TOI.The reunion with Jalaj, one of the pillars of Kerala cricket for close to a decade, also restores a partnership that Sarwate cherishes.“I am looking forward to bowling in tandem with Jalaj bhai. He is a true legend,” Sarwate said. “I have picked up details about the game after bowling with him. His game awareness, field placements and building pressure on the opposition are top-notch.”Jalaj, the off-spinner, and Sarwate, the left-arm spinner give Kerala attack the ammunition it requires to go the distance this season. Kerala pacer MD Nidheesh, currently in Chennai with the Duleep Trophy squad, knows what Kerala missed in their absence last season.“With their return, it feels like the good old days,” Nideesh offered. “We missed Jalaj bhai and Aditya last season, especially on pitches that aided spin,” he elaborated.Jalaj moved to Maharashtra last season after obtaining the NOC from the KCA, citing personal reasons. “Once his personal issues were sorted, he chose to come back to the team that has been his home for close to a decade,” KCA secretary Vinod S Kumar said.The return of these two spinners comes when Kerala wants a stronger push after a modest 2025-26 league season, where they finished Elite Group B with one win, two losses and four draws from seven games.The new season starts on Oct 11 when Kerala plays Jharkhand.Before that, Sarwate is poised to feature in Kerala’s two practice games against Jammu & Kashmir in Srinagar from Sept 11, as part of the team’s preparations for the Ranji season.New Kerala coach announcement soonThe KCA is set to announce the head coach for the Kerala Ranji Trophy team soon, with a top official stating it would be done by the end of this week.“We were waiting for the KCL to get over. The core committee has already met candidates and meetings are taking place. We expect an announcement in a couple of days, latest by the end of this week,” Kumar added.Khurasiya, the former India international who guided Kerala to their maiden Ranji Trophy final two years ago, stepped down as head coach at the end of the previous season after the completion of his two-year tenure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Clarke leads Notts recovery against Hampshire
articles.summary: Joe Clarke scores 105 as title hopefuls Nottinghamshire recover from 20-3 to total 377 on the first day against Hampshire.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Trent Bridge (day one)

Nottinghamshire 377: Clarke 105, Patterson-White 92; Currie 4-61, Abbott 4-82

Joe Clarke's fourth hundred of an outstanding campaign revived champions Nottinghamshire from early peril after Kyle Abbott's three morning wickets helped take his season's tally for Hampshire to 57.

Nottinghamshire, four points behind County Championship leaders Somerset at the close, posted 377 at Trent Bridge against visitors Hampshire who remain in danger of returning to Division Two for the first time since 2014. They were 12-0 at the close

Though buoyed perhaps by the news that Leicestershire may face a loss of points for their Grace Road pitch, and no decision has yet been announced regarding a possible penalty for Surrey too, Hampshire still need to close an improbable 30-point gap to be safe.

No such worries for Nottinghamshire as Clarke moved to 105, adding 78 for the third wicket with Jack Haynes (48) and 136 with Mitchell Hay for the fourth as the Kiwi, his side's fifth overseas signing this summer, made 49 on county debut. Liam Patterson-White's (92) late onslaught cemented three batting points.

Nottinghamshire add Hay as Verreynne replacement

Leicestershire charged over Grace Road pitch

It seemed either reckless or bold first thing that Notts should unveil an emerald green pitch against an attack led by Abbott, one of the most successful overseas seamers ever to grace the circuit. Within eight overs, put in, they were 20-3. Abbott removed Haseeb and Freddie McCann before Ben Slater skied a pull off Scott Currie, each going for single figures.

Slater had earlier taken a withering blow to the arm when defending himself against a chest-high full toss from Eddie Jack only to fall, after a long stoppage, four overs later. At that point neither new batter had faced and indeed Clarke took 22 balls to get off the mark.

Haynes, however, feasted on Jack, wayward on the eve of his 21st birthday, and at one point took two sixes and a four in four balls from debutant seamer Manny Lumsden, so impressive for England Under-19 in their victory over Pakistan in the youth Test last week but sorely punished here.

After 64 had been plundered in eight overs, Abbott, now in his fortieth year, returned to undo Haynes for 48 from 46 balls as lunch came at 106-4. He should have claimed another when Hay, on 29, was missed at second slip in the afternoon.

For all his repute as a white-ball dasher, the New Zealander was impressively content to bed in, supporting Clarke until cutting at a lifting ball from Jack and edging behind 25 minutes from tea.

Clarke, then 99, completed his century from 159 balls next over but, driving at Currie, he gave wicketkeeper Ben Brown his fifth catch. A first batting point had just been secured by the interval on 262-6.

Hay's Canterbury team-mate back home, Fraser Sheat, out for five, soon brought Abbott's next success on resumption but Patterson-White, fresh from a not-out hundred in his last innings five days earlier, added 44 with Olly Stone who provided Lumsden with his maiden wicket in finding Brown's gloves yet again.

The third delivery with the new ball, taken immediately, denied Abbott his five-wicket bag when Dillon Pennington escaped on four.

The reprieve was costly: the ninth wicket added another 39 (47 from seven overs) before Pennington fell swiping at Currie who took the running catch at cover off his own bowling as Patterson-White's skier, with nine men on the boundary, finally ended his carnage.

He had overseen 112 runs from the last three wickets against a wilting attack, though Currie at least had the slightly flattering consolation of 4-61.

articles.title: Warwickshire turn up the heat on Somerset and Nottingham in County Championship as they inflict Glamorgan 19-year first
articles.summary: The Rothesay County Championship title chase cranked up as Warwickshire dominated in Wales; Division Two Durham were put to the test by Middlesex before pulling off impressive comeback
articles.body:
Just five points separate the Bears from leaders Somerset and Nottinghamshire heading into the last three fixtures, and Ethan Bamber took a scintillating 5-28 that took him past 50 wickets for the season.

Ed Barnard backed him up with 3-5 against the tail as the first innings concluded inside just 27 overs.

Warwickshire were in complete control on 129-3 by stumps, with Will Young dismissed for 60 and almost overtaking the home side's score on his own.

This was Glamorgan's lowest score since being bowled out for 60 against Middlesex in 2007.

Leaders Somerset - who are looking to claim a first County Championship title - were in total control against Leicestershire, with Josh Thomas making exactly 100 as he led an opening stand of 181 with Tom Lammonby (74), with James Rew holding up a faltering middle order.

Defending champions Nottinghamshire were 98-4 against bottom side Hampshire at Trent Bridge, but recovered to 377 all out, thanks in large part to Joe Clarke's 105 who extended his position as the highest run-scorer in the top flight.

At Headingley, Yorkshire managed a 241-6 against Essex, while there was no play possible at Hove between Surrey and Sussex due to the weather.

Brydon Carse takes two wickets in Division Two as Durham forced to fight back against Middlesex

Middlesex had Divison Two leaders Durham 80-4 in their opening fixture as Seb Morgan took four wickets, with two coming from just three balls.

Durham came back through a wicket stand of 90 between Ben Raine and Callum Parkinson before being bowled out for 252.

Brydon Carse came in for Middlesex and took both wickets as they reached 52-2 in reply at Chester-le-Street, ending the day trailing by 182 runs.

Fellow promotion hopefuls Kent were 11-1 at stumps after bowling hosts Derbyshire out for 300, with third-placed Northamptonshire 13 without loss having knocked over Worcestershire for 200.

articles.title: ‘The series is lost but we have nothing to lose’: Babar Azam rallies Pakistan for Edgbaston Test against England
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has urged his reshaped side to play without fear in the third and final Test against England, insisting there is little le.
articles.body: Pakistan captain Babar Azam has urged his reshaped side to play without fear in the third and final Test against England, insisting there is little left to lose after a dramatic mid-series overhaul by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).Pakistan trail 0-2 after heavy defeats at Headingley and Lord’s, with the PCB responding by releasing seven players from the touring squad and removing head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul. Five players without Test experience have been brought into the squad, while Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke have taken charge for the Edgbaston Test.With Pakistan already out of contention for the series, Babar believes the upheaval can instead give the newcomers a chance to make an impact.‘We should play freely’“The series is lost but we have nothing to lose,” Babar said on the eve of the Test. “We should play freely and believe in ourselves as a team.”Babar revealed that the sweeping changes came as a surprise to him, with the captain learning about the PCB's decisions only after they had been announced.“It was news to me,” he said. “I found out after.“The PCB decided it, so they will be able to explain better. The PCB's decision must have been taken after some thought process. It's better if you ask them why.”The captain, however, said the new-look squad should embrace the opportunity rather than dwell on the turmoil surrounding the side.“We've practised a couple of days and explained things to the new boys. Any young player who comes in is excited, and that excitement is visible. I believe that will be visible in the match, too,” he added.Babar also accepted that Pakistan had failed to deliver across the first two Tests, while defending the thinking behind the selections that were made.“We didn't play well in all three facets as a team,” he said. “And when you don't get results, then you'll get plenty of criticism from outside. But we did what we thought was best at the time.”He added: “The way we read the pitch and conditions, the XIs we went with were what we thought was best at the time. But we did not get the results or performance we expected of ourselves.”Babar missed the innings defeat at Headingley with a finger injury before returning at Lord’s, where he scored only eight and six as Pakistan suffered a 194-run loss. He called on the senior players to set the tone in Birmingham.“I firmly believe you need to grab opportunities and perform in difficult conditions,” Babar said. “That's why we play cricket, because we have to perform and dominate in difficult conditions. We need to forget about past failures and shift focus to the future,” he said.Babar's comments on the shake-upThe Pakistan captain's revelation that the squad overhaul was “news to me” added another layer to the crisis engulfing the side. The PCB released Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Agha, Ali Usman, Aamer Jamal, Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad from the squad following the Lord’s defeat.Babar, though, said the board would have to explain the reasoning behind the decisions, while he would focus on leading the players available to him.The PCB has also confirmed an internal disciplinary inquiry into reports concerning “discipline and conduct”, adding further uncertainty around the team ahead of the final Test.England captain Joe Root, meanwhile, rejected the suggestion that Pakistan had lacked fight during the series.“We've found Pakistan a challenge,” Root said. “I think that's a bit disrespectful to both Pakistan as a team and to us as a team.“I don't think we've allowed them to get into games because of how well we've played and how quickly we've read the situations and the surfaces that we've had.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'I knew before the series': Wasim Akram predicts Pakistan's 3-0 England whitewash
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram said he knew before the ongoing Test series in England that Pakistan would lose 3-0. Pakistan have stru.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram said he knew before the ongoing Test series in England that Pakistan would lose 3-0. Pakistan have struggled to challenge England in the first two Tests and trail 0-2 going into the third and final Test, starting on Wednesday.“I knew before the series we were going to lose 3-0 to England,” Akram is quoted as saying by The Athletic. “Our batting is struggling, our bowling is below average and our fielding is worse. It’s not rocket science.”Akram was an important part of the Pakistan team that won three straight Test series in England in 1987 and 1996. He was also Pakistan's captain in the last of those consecutive series wins.Akram reacts to PCB's major changesPakistan's poor performances have attracted criticism, but the Pakistan Cricket Board's major changes after the second Test have also shocked the cricket world.The PCB sent seven players from the squad back home and sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and his staff after the second Test.Akram said he feels for the players, but believes their attitude is also part of the problem.“But in Pakistan we have a saying: ‘You can only clap with two hands’,” he said. “I get asked all the time, ‘Can you do something to help Pakistan cricket?’ But the issues are a lot deeper. These are the top players, there’s nothing else there. The systems aren’t there below that. The first-class structure domestically has been all over the place the last few years and there’s no consistency, no patience.“That dribbles down to the fans, too. They see the team lose and they want to rip it all up, too. We’ve done that so many times and now there is nothing really left,” said Akram.‘There can be no compromise’ on Imran Khan's healthAkram also spoke about his friend and former Pakistan captain Imran Khan and raised concerns about his health. Akram said he has not spoken to Imran for three years and expressed worry about what is happening to him."I haven't spoken to him for three years. articles.title: 'Disrespectful' to say Pakistan showed no fight: Joe Root defends Babar Azam's side ahead of third Test
articles.summary: Cricket News: England captain Joe Root has defended Pakistan ahead of the third Test at Edgbaston, saying it is \"disrespectful\" to claim the visitors have shown \"no.
articles.body: England captain Joe Root has defended Pakistan ahead of the third Test at Edgbaston, saying it is "disrespectful" to claim the visitors have shown "no fight" despite trailing 2-0 in the three-match series.England have already sealed the series after an innings-and-103-run win at Headingley and a 194-run victory at Lord's. Pakistan have failed to score 200 in any of their four innings so far against England's pace attack of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.Pakistan head into the final Test after a major shake-up in the squad and coaching staff. The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sent seven players home after the Lord's defeat, removed Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed, and brought in white-ball coach Mike Hesson to lead the side for the series finale. The board also added seven players to the squad, including five uncapped Test cricketers.The team has been labelled one of Pakistan's weakest Test sides in decades, but Root rejected the suggestion that England had faced an opposition lacking fight.Asked during his pre-match press conference ahead of the third Test on what it was like to play against a team offering "no fight", Root pushed back strongly."Absolutely we have found (Pakistan) a challenge," Root said."I think that's a bit disrespectful to both Pakistan as a team and to us as a team. I don't think we've allowed them to get into games because of how well we've played as well and how quickly we've read the situations and the surfaces that we've had," the England captain said."I think it's very easy to say one team is excellent and one team is poor. Normally it's somewhere in the middle."The England skipper said performances should not be viewed in extremes and credited his own team for taking control of the first two Tests."If one team has been outstanding then the other team can't have been poor and vice-versa. I think it's important to live in that middle area somewhere and understand that that's not how it is," Root added."Regardless of what's happened over the last two games, this week it's a completely different proposition for us."Root also warned his players against taking Pakistan lightly despite the visitors' struggles in the series."There's a very talented group of players in that dressing room and you've got to be ready for it, so we'll make sure that we are."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Duleep Trophy final: Mukesh Kumar, Mohammed Shami help East take control
articles.summary: Cricket News: CHENNAI: Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar may currently find themselves outside India's red-ball set-up, but the two Bengal pacers offered a timely rem.
articles.body: CHENNAI: Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar may currently find themselves outside India's red-ball set-up, but the two Bengal pacers offered a timely reminder of their quality on a flat MA Chidambaram Stadium surface on Tuesday.Bowling in Chennai heat, Shami and Mukesh combined for four wickets as East Zone tightened their grip over the Duleep Trophy final. South Zone ended Day Three on 242-6, still trailing by 466 runs after East had posted a mammoth first-innings total.Shami (2-17 in 11 overs) showed superb control as he went on to pick the wickets of well-set Shaikh Rasheed and Smaran Ravichandran, both talented players from the South stable. Mukesh, on the other hand, returned figures of 2-36 from 12 overs. The pair complemented each other beautifully, constantly discussing what length to bowl, and used reverse swing smartly."After roughly 20 overs, there was a little bit of movement - reverse and otherwise. We benefited from that, so we were able to pick up wickets quickly," Mukesh said at the end of day's play.East captain Ishan Kishan was careful with his premier seamers, aware of the physical demands of bowling in humid conditions. Shami opened with a three-over spell that cost just one run, while Mukesh bowled four and removed Ricky Bhui, who edged a delivery that zipped down the leg side to Kumar Kushagra."It is very hot here right now, and the wicket is flat. So, five or six-over spells wouldn't really work here...In fact, long spells can lead to cramps," Mukesh said. "Our plan as a team was to bowl in short bursts...We put in maximum effort into every ball. That worked out well for us."With left-arm spinner Anukul Roy unable to bowl after injuring his bowling hand on Monday, East had to rely on part-time spin.Shikhar Mohan, bowling left-arm orthodox in Anukul's absence, made the most of his opportunity by claiming his maiden first-class wicket when N Jagadeesan (32) sliced a delivery to Abhimanyu Easwaran at backward point.Devdutt Padikkal, fresh from his impressive India performances, reached his half-century off 65 balls but his partnership with Rasheed was broken by Shami. The veteran paceman returned after lunch to dismiss the right-hander, nipping one back sharply to trap him leg-before.Mukesh, also created considerable pressure and picked the prized scalp of Padikkal, who fell for 62. "The plan against Devdutt was to bowl stump-to-stump," Mukesh said. "On wickets like this, if you offer width to batters, runs will leak. Our plan was to stay consistent, bowl dot balls and let them take the risks."The key, Mukesh explained, was not trying to overdo things on a flat pitch. "Speed was a priority, but without fitness you can't increase pace. Then it is about hitting the deck and gauging the length that works on this pitch," he said.Tilak Varma's unbeaten 56 offered South some resistance, with Shreyas Gopal adding 38 before falling to Kounain Quraishi in the last over of the day.Brief scores:East Zone 708 all out. South Zone 242-6 (Padikkal 62, Tilak 56*). Match to continue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Rana suffered a hamstring injury during the England tour in July, while Reddy missed both the UK and Sri Lanka tours due to a quadriceps injury.India had named a full-strength squad, led by Shreyas Iyer, for the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, with star allrounder Hardik Pandya the notable absentee as he continues to recover from injury. articles.title: Why shouldn’t National Sports Governance Act apply to BCCI, state bodies, asks Supreme Court
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Tired of handling lingering litigations in cricket management for 12 years since it took up and ushered in reforms in the world’s richest c.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tired of handling lingering litigations in cricket management for 12 years since it took up and ushered in reforms in the world’s richest cricket organisation, the Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Board of Control for Cricket in India and state associations why they should not be brought under National Sports Governance (NSG) Act, 2025.With multiple applications by different state cricket associations and their members either for minor changes in their constitution, or disputes arising from factionalism over control over the cash-rich cricket management bodies, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana in a cryptic order at the fag-end of the day’s proceedings asked the BCCI and state affiliates why they should not be governed by the NSG Act and sought their responses.The flow of the applications in the original petition filed by BCCI in 2014, which led to framing of its constitution in August 2018 by the SC on the recommendations of Justice R M Lodha committee, continued even after the SC permitted significant amendments to the BCCI constitution in Sept 2022 relating to consecutive terms of the office bearers and cooling off period terms in office.In May this year, the sports ministry notified new rules under the NSG Act to improve management of sports bodies and adjudication of disputes. If the BCCI and state cricket associations agree to be covered under the NSG Act and the Rules framed thereunder, then all the litigation pending before the SC relating to the functioning and management of cricket bodies would get transferred to the sports tribunal, easing a considerable load off the already overburdened SC.NSG Act and Rules mandate a National Sports Board as the central regulatory authority responsible for recognising national sports bodies and monitoring compliance with governance, financial, and ethical standards. These also provide processes for transparent elections and tenure of elected office bearers.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BCCI relents on Asian Games stay, agrees to stay in designated hotels
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Indian cricket board (BCCI) has relented on the accommodation issue for the Asian Games, agreeing that the country's cricketers will st.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian cricket board (BCCI) has relented on the accommodation issue for the Asian Games, agreeing that the country's cricketers will stay in the official hotels designated by the Aichi-Nagoya organisers. The players will not be accommodated in an alternative hotel, BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla confirmed on Tuesday.While the organisers' allocation had raised concerns over twin-sharing rooms, Shukla said the board would look to get its cricketers individual rooms in the official hotels. "Whatever they (organisers) are providing, we are staying there. We have photographs and videos of the accommodation and, though it is not five-star, it is good and comfortable. The options were to make them stay in Osaka or Tokyo, but that's too far away," Shukla said at the Asian Games-bound Indian contingent's send-off ceremony here. The men's team has been allotted the three-star APA Hotel Nagoya Ekimae, while the women's team will stay at the four-star Meitetsu Grand Hotel. Both are below the five-star standard Indian cricketers usually receive on overseas tours.Shukla said the bigger concern was the playing facilities. "The big issue was the ground, wickets and dressing rooms. The Asian Cricket Council's (ACC) team visited Nagoya and is now satisfied with the facilities," he said. TOI had reported on Saturday, quoting Indian Olympic Association (IOA) CEO Raghuram Iyer, that the cricketers would not receive special treatment.The IOA had said it would not seek separate arrangements for cricket.Shukla also dismissed speculation that India would send a second-string side. “It is a complete rumour that we are sending our ‘B’ team. Our full contingent is going with the most talented players, and I hope we will definitely win,” he said.IOA president PT Usha confirmed the issue had been resolved. “There’s no problem and everything is sorted,” she added.India are the defending champions in both men's and women's events.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: KOLKATA: East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan’s monumental 270 off 334 balls in the Duleep Trophy final has strengthened his case for a return to the Indian.
articles.body: KOLKATA: East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan’s monumental 270 off 334 balls in the Duleep Trophy final has strengthened his case for a return to the Indian Test side, with the Jharkhand wicketkeeper-batter now emerging as a genuine all-format option after an impressive run in international as well as domestic cricket.The innings against South Zone in Chennai was more than just a big score. Coming after a season in which Ishan has consistently delivered in both white-ball and red-ball cricket, it offered a strong indication that he has developed the temperament and game to succeed in the longest format.Former India wicketkeeper Saba Karim believes Ishan’s recent progress reflects a greater maturity in his approach to the game.“The work Ishan has put in at the domestic level over the last season reflects his growing maturity and his desire to be a part of Indian cricket across all three formats. It is good to see him understand his game better and keep improving. The hard work and introspection he has invested in his cricket are now showing in his performances,” Karim told TOI on Tuesday.The conditions made the 270 even more significant. Ishan spent more than nine hours over two days at the crease in Chennai’s heat and humidity, against a strong South Zone attack, to produce one of the most emphatic red-ball statements of his career.“To score 270 in a Duleep Trophy final against a strong South Zone side speaks volumes about his development as a red-ball cricketer. Doing it in Chennai, where the conditions are extremely hot and humid, makes the effort even more special. It was a remarkable innings and I am delighted for him,” Karim said.Former India batter Saurabh Tiwary, Ishan’s senior teammate for Jharkhand, believes the Duleep Trophy performance is a continuation of a broader resurgence rather than an isolated effort. Ishan has also been among the runs in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, his highest of the season being 173 from 247 deliveries against Tamil Nadu, in tough batting conditions in Coimbatore.“He has been doing well for some time now, and I can say he is having a golden touch,” Tiwary said. “What’s important is that he has performed not only in white-ball cricket but also in red-ball cricket.”That consistency has now put the Test door firmly within reach.“There is tremendous competition in the Indian team, and it’s never easy to secure a place, but he is certainly knocking on the door,” Tiwary said.Karim feels Ishan’s value to India goes beyond his wicketkeeping credentials, particularly given his ability to contribute in different roles.“Now, with the runs he has scored in red-ball cricket, the Indian team will certainly view him as a strong option in the Test format as well. If your batting is good enough, you can always earn a place as a specialist batter, even if you are primarily known as a wicketkeeper,” he said.The transformation has come through a return to the domestic grind following a season without a BCCI central contract.“One of the most important aspects of a cricketer’s career is responding to setbacks. If you are out of the team, you have to go back to domestic cricket, work hard and become the best performer you can be. Ishan has followed that path,” Karim said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: The famous India vs Pakistan moment: When Sunil Gavaskar put his foot over the toss coin
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: A toss before an India vs Pakistan match is always special. But one toss from 1984 has remained memorable for a very different reason.On Ap.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A toss before an India vs Pakistan match is always special. But one toss from 1984 has remained memorable for a very different reason.On April 13, 1984, India and Pakistan met at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates during the inaugural Asia Cup.India captain Sunil Gavaskar and Pakistan captain Zaheer Abbas were at the centre of a light-hearted moment before the match. As the toss took place, Gavaskar jokingly put his foot over the coin, creating a candid moment between the two captains.The match was part of the first-ever Asia Cup, which featured only three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India 188/4 in 46 oversIndia won the toss and decided to bat first and scored 188/4 in 46 overs. Surinder Khanna was India's top scorer with 56 off 72 balls. Sandeep Patil added 43 off 50 balls. Gavaskar stayed unbeaten on 36 off 55 balls. Ghulam Parkar scored 22, while Dilip Vengsarkar made 14.Pakistan's bowlers picked up four wickets, with Shahid Mahboob, Mudassar Nazar and Sarfraz Nawaz among those to take wickets.Pakistan collapse in the chasePakistan's chase never gathered momentum. They were bowled out for 134 in 39.4 overs.Mohsin Khan top-scored with 35, while Zaheer Abbas made 27. Qasim Umar scored 16 and Saleem Malik made 15, but Pakistan lost wickets regularly.India's bowlers played a major role in the collapse.Roger Binny and Ravi Shastri took three wickets each. Binny finished with 3/33, while Shastri returned figures of 3/40.Pakistan were eventually dismissed for 134, handing India a big victory.India win the first Asia CupIndia went on to win the first Asia Cup title. The 1984 tournament had just three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India lead the Asia Cup title raceIndia have since become the most successful team in Asia Cup history based on the title record provided. articles.title: India's New Zealand tour: Over 50,000 tickets sold in just two weeks
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The upcoming India tour of New Zealand has already created strong interest among fans, with more than 50,000 tickets sold in just over two .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The upcoming India tour of New Zealand has already created strong interest among fans, with more than 50,000 tickets sold in just over two weeks.India will tour New Zealand for the first time in six years. The teams will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Test matches during the tour.The strong ticket sales have given New Zealand Cricket (NZC) a boost ahead of the much-awaited series.Several matches close to a sell-outTicket sales opened to the public on Monday after a two-week pre-sale period for Cricket Nation members, Sky customers and ANZ customers.According to a press release: "Ticket sales opened to the public on Monday after a two week pre-sale window for Cricket Nation members, Sky customers, and ANZ customers, with several matches on track to sell out, including the second T20I against India in Christchurch which sits at 75% sold out."Demand has also been high at Eden Park. NZC has opened the stadium's sixth tier of seating for the first time since India's 2019 tour of New Zealand.The upper level will be available for the fourth T20I against India on Friday, October 30."High demand at Eden Park has required the stadium's sixth tier of seating to open for the first time since the 2019 India tour of New Zealand, with the upper level available for the fourth T20I against India on Friday 30 October," the release further stated.NZC excited by the responseNZC Head of Marketing Tim Ellis said the excitement around India's tour was growing."Being able to open up the top level of Eden Park for the first time in years is really exciting and speaks to the swell of excitement building around the tour. Matches at Hagley Oval have always been well attended but to have one of them over three quarters sold already is quite remarkable," Ellis was quoted as saying in the release.Ellis also said NZC was working on several events and activities for fans during the tour."We're deep into planning for a number of events surrounding the tour and have some exciting at-game activations in the works that we're confident will deliver a great experience for fans of all ages," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
